description: Loose Ends — reads anything new in the ledger and opens what is genuinely unfinished. Runs when new interactions arrive and again each evening.
name: autopilot_loose_ends

nodes.label: Anything to read, and a reader free?
Anything for a model to sort?

message.value:
Sort new mail into two piles, Read or Noise. That is all you do in this run: do not write commitments, people or anything else, do not open mail bodies beyond the opening lines you are given, and do not inspect functions, tables or files.

1. Get what is waiting: `lemma functions run triage --data '{"mode":"list"}' --output json`. Each entry is one conversation from somebody the person has never written to and has not answered: `thread`, `sender`, `subject`, `opening`.
2. Decide each one.
   NOISE: a newsletter, product update, notification, receipt, automated alert, event promotion, or a cold pitch — a stranger selling a product or service, an agency offering candidates, design, SEO or development work, or an unsolicited investment or partnership template.
   READ: a real person asking this person for something or answering something; a customer, candidate, investor, partner or supplier writing for the first time about real business; anything about money owed, a contract, a deadline, legal or the security of their own accounts. A first message from a stranger that asks a specific question about the person's own product or work is READ, not a pitch.
   If you are not sure, it is READ. Wrongly reading costs a minute; wrongly discarding hides something from them.
3. Save every verdict in ONE call: write verdicts.json as {"mode":"apply","verdicts":[{"thread":"<thread>","noise":true,"reason":"cold pitch for SEO services"},{"thread":"<thread>","noise":false}]} and run `lemma functions run triage --data @verdicts.json --output json`. Give each NOISE a reason of a few plain words.
4. Reply with the two counts only.

nodes.label: Sort the rest into Read or Noise

message.value: Load the otto-notice skill and follow it exactly. Read the unread rows in the interaction ledger and turn them into commitments, people, companies, timeline entries and board cards. Only open commitments from the last three weeks. Filter cold outbound aggressively. Never open a commitment you were only copied on. Check what is already open before writing anything so the same obligation never becomes a second row. Write through ingest_open_loops and mark everything you read with mark_extracted, including the noise. Do not send anything. Report totals only. Start reading straight away: do not inspect functions, tables or files first. When pending_interactions returns no rows, stop at once and do nothing else.

Load the otto-write skill and follow it exactly — including reading /me/voice.md and settings voice_doc before writing anything.

Find every open commitment on the person's own side (`loops.side='you'`, `status='open'`) that has no pending row in `drafts`, and prepare it. Newest first, stop after eight.

For each, decide the shape the skill describes:
- email — the answer is something said. Fill kind='email', subject, body, to_emails, cc_emails.
- meeting — a call was agreed or would settle it. Call find_free_slots and fill kind='meeting' with a `meeting` JSON of 2–4 real slots, plus a short covering body.
- document — what was promised is a thing (offer letter, JD, proposal, LOI, specs). Write the complete document into `deliverables` (kind='doc', status='pending', loop_id) and an email draft (kind='email') that sends it.

Always set `note` to one past-tense line saying what you prepared. One pending draft per commitment — update rather than adding a second. Never send anything. Never invent a fact; mark a genuine unknown with [...] and say so in the note. Report how many you prepared of each shape.
